niche: a port authority's on-road NOx inventory for the roadway links around its terminals, each link's program-year vehicle-miles by class expanded from short-duration classification counts with the state's continuous count stations, to designate links for its 2027 air-corridor program
answer: Designate four of the fourteen port roadway links: L01, L03, L05 and L14 (the all-vehicle expansion designates ten).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the three count programmes and the station records, reads every field and rule correctly and expands each link's count with the stations' all-vehicle factors, splitting by the counted class shares, designates L01, L03, L04, L05, L06, L09, L10, L11, L13 and L14; only expanding each class with its own factors from the classifying stations designates L01, L03, L05 and L14.
domain_test: The decisive quantity is each link's program-year NOx per mile, an on-road inventory's vehicle-miles by class times class emission rates, where annual vehicle-miles come from short counts expanded by temporal factors from continuous count stations (the traffic monitoring guide's method); the textbook applies one set of factors to all vehicles, which the classification stations show fails for trucks.
layer2_pattern: own:class-specific temporal expansion of short counts, the all-vehicle factor assumption broken for trucks and measured by the classification stations

world.geography: United States, a fictional coastal metropolitan area

driver: A period total at each site is estimated from a two-day sample expanded by calendar factors measured at always-on reference sites, and the factors differ by class of contributor: the heaviest-emitting class falls away at weekends and barely moves by season, so expanding a weekday sample with factors for all contributors and splitting by the sampled class share overstates that class at every site; the classes are expanded separately with factors from the reference sites that classify.
driver_concrete: Each roadway link's NOx per mile for October 2025 to September 2026 is passenger-vehicle and truck miles times their emission rates, the miles expanded from the link's 48-hour classification count with monthly and day-of-week factors computed separately for cars and trucks at the state's classification stations, not with the all-vehicle factors of every station.
stump: The default path expands each link's two-weekday count with the stations' all-vehicle monthly and day-of-week factors and splits it by the counted truck share, designating L01, L03, L04, L05, L06, L09, L10, L11, L13 and L14; trucks run about a quarter above their annual average on weekdays and fall away at weekends while cars barely move, so only expanding each class with its own factors from the classifying stations designates L01, L03, L05 and L14.

lineage.driver: A unit's period total is measured hourly by an instrument that shares a utility with the unit's control device, so when the utility fails the instrument goes dark while the control is off; the dark hours are filled at the uncontrolled level the instrument reads in its first hours back, times the hour's metered input, rather than from the unit's measured hours in the same operating state or from the hours either side, which the controlled hours dominate.
lineage.stump: The default path fills every unmonitored hour from the unit's own measured hours in the same start state and load, and designates AF-2, CB-1, DF-1, DF-3 and SR-1; the gaps that came with the plants' instrument air trips are hours when the SCR's air-operated ammonia valves had closed as well, which the first measured hour after each trip shows at about twenty times the controlled rate, so filling those hours at that uncontrolled level adds CB-2 and AF-1.

lineage.driver: A unit's period total is measured hourly by an instrument that is out mostly in the hours after the unit starts, when the quantity runs several times its steady level at the same operating point, so the missing hours are filled by the hour's start state, read from an every-hour operating log, rather than by a fit on the operating point that the steady hours dominate.
lineage.stump: The default path fills each unmonitored hour from the unit's NOx-on-load regression and designates the units that run steadily high, because the analyzers drop out mostly right after a start, when the cold catalyst lets NOx run at several times the steady rate; filling the missing hours by hours since start designates the hard-cycling units the program should fund.
